alerts.title: EFV neuropsychiatric toxicity: insomnia and vivid dreams
alerts.message: Guidelines note EFV frequently causes neuropsychiatric effects including insomnia, vivid dreams and dizziness, typically within the first 2-6 weeks of therapy. This patient started EFV in February 2024 and now reports several weeks of poor sleep and vivid dreams, which are classic EFV toxicity symptoms listed in the adverse event monitoring checklist. Evidence for drug attribution: symptoms match the guideline-described EFV toxicity profile exactly. Evidence against: onset is late relative to the typical 2-6 week window, and non-drug causes such as depression, anxiety or substance use have not been excluded. The clinician's plan documents the complaint but proposes no management or regimen change.

evidence.recommended_action: Screen for depression, anxiety and substance use using validated tools; consider EFV substitution per guideline toxicity management if symptoms persist or worsen.

alerts.title: Neuropsychiatric adverse event not flagged for aDSM reporting
alerts.message: Guidelines require active screening for neuropsychiatric symptoms including bad dreams, insomnia, anxiety and mood changes at every visit for patients on EFV, with suspected adverse drug reactions documented and reported through adverse drug surveillance (aDSM) channels. This patient's insomnia and vivid dreams were recorded at intake but no adverse event documentation, reporting form, or follow-up monitoring plan appears in today's assessment. The encounter also lacks any mental health screening despite guideline emphasis on diagnosing depression and anxiety with brief validated instruments.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete suspected ADR documentation and submit the aDSM form; schedule symptom reassessment at next visit.
